jobs.description: Career Spotlight: Building from the ground up - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: Building from the ground up By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Lirit Tsimerman, VP of Deal Desk (Sales) When I joined WalkMe as Director of the Commercial Desk, I wasn’t looking to just manage a team, I wanted to build something from the ground up. My first months were all about rolling up my sleeves: learning how the desk supported Sales, where the bottlenecks were, and where we could do better. I’ve always believed the best way to lead is to understand the work firsthand, so that’s exactly what I did. Table of Contents hide From vision to reality Redefining revenue operations A culture that trusts you to dream big What keeps me going Looking back From vision to reality Two years in, I started putting my vision into action. We introduced a quoting tool (CPQ), stood up a dedicated Order Management team, and drew a clear line between OM and Deal Desk responsibilities. Together, we mapped the entire Quote-to-Cash process, built cross-departmental collaboration, and created a workflow that finally felt like it worked for Sales instead of against them. As WalkMe grew, so did my role. I led process innovation, supported global operations, and worked to bring different teams around shared goals. Recently, I was promoted to Vice President, something I see not just as recognition of my growth but of the trust WalkMe has shown me throughout this journey. Redefining revenue operations One of the milestones I’m most proud of has been building two high-performing teams, Deal Desk and Order Management, from scratch. Today, they’re not only trusted advisors to Sales but also key collaborators with Legal, Rev Rec, Billing, and Collections. It wasn’t always that way. When I started, Sales was hesitant to approach Deal Desk. Fast forward a few years, and we’ve become their go-to team, even for questions outside our direct scope. That shift, from avoidance to confidence, is one of my proudest achievements. A standout project was creating the Order Management team. By separating its role from Deal Desk, hiring the right people, and designing a seamless handoff, we brought clarity, balance, and focus to our operations. Both teams are thriving today in their own lanes. A culture that trusts you to dream big From day one, I felt empowered to take big swings and make meaningful change. Even when change came with growing pains, I was trusted, heard, and supported. That support extended outside of work too. Over these years, I’ve not only grown professionally but also built a family. WalkMe’s people-first culture and commitment to work-life balance made that possible. What keeps me going The people. The pace. The possibility. Every day brings something new, and that momentum is energizing. We’re always pushing forward, adopting new technologies like AI, optimizing processes, and finding smarter, faster ways to work. One of our values, Act with Empathy, resonates deeply with me. It’s not just a phrase on a wall, it’s how we collaborate, lead, and show up for one another as colleagues and as people. Looking back How would I summarize my WalkMe journey? There is no better place to learn, dream, achieve, and develop. The trust I’ve been given, the freedom to grow, and the amazing people I work with every day make this place special. It’s never boring, we’re always evolving, and that momentum keeps me motivated. jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From law to leadership - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: From law to leadership By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Gil Wiener, DeepUI Solutions Engineering Manager When I joined WalkMe, I was making a big leap, moving from four years in the alternative investment industry with degrees in Business and Law into an entirely new world: tech. I had no background in engineering or software, but after taking a series of relevant courses, I felt ready to shift directions. WalkMe took a chance on me, bringing me on as a DeepUI Solution Engineer, and that opportunity truly changed the trajectory of my career. Table of Contents hide Finding my footing Defining moments A culture that encourages growth Looking ahead Finding my footing In that first role, I focused heavily on log analysis and content performance, helping ensure WalkMe’s product worked seamlessly for our customers. It was all new to me, but I was eager to learn. Over time, I moved into a Team Lead position, and eventually into my current role as Group Manager, where I now lead a global team. As I’ve grown, so has the scope of my work. I’ve gone from tactical execution to strategic leadership. Today, I focus on cross-functional collaboration, mentorship, and driving innovation across our product and internal operations, especially through the integration of Generative AI. Defining moments Stepping into group leadership has been a defining milestone. It has allowed me to scale the team, develop future leaders, and contribute to WalkMe’s broader product strategy in a meaningful way. One project I’m especially proud of was automating a time-consuming, manual process that was slowing us down. What started as a challenge quickly became an opportunity to think bigger. By streamlining workflows and implementing the right tools, we significantly expanded our team’s capacity and freed people to focus on more strategic work. It was a powerful reminder of the impact of zooming out, spotting inefficiencies, and solving creatively. A culture that encourages growth WalkMe has supported my career every step of the way: through technical training, leadership development, mentorship, and most importantly, the freedom to explore and innovate. My managers and senior leaders have consistently encouraged me to take risks, pursue new ideas, and grow into each role with confidence. What’s kept me here for five years? The people. I work alongside incredibly smart, thoughtful, and driven colleagues who challenge and inspire me daily. I also feel truly seen and supported, from peers to executives, and that kind of culture is rare. Looking ahead In the next 5 to 10 years, I see myself stepping further into senior leadership, helping shape long-term strategy and scaling global programs with real impact. I’m especially passionate about mentoring others and embedding AI and automation into how we operate. Not just to move faster, but to work smarter and better. What keeps me motivated every day is the variety. No two days are the same. There are always new challenges, new opportunities, and the chance to grow and make an impact. How would I sum up my WalkMe journey? A dynamic evolution marked by continuous learning, impactful leadership, and a deep commitment to innovation and growth. Want to join Gil and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From the front lines to VP - WalkMe Blog Home » WalkMe Company News Career Spotlight: From the front lines to VP By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Nate Campbell, VP Customer Success Americas When I first discovered WalkMe, it wasn’t through a job board. It was at my previous company, where WalkMe was the only tool that helped us scale. I remember thinking, “This is something special.” At the time, I had only been in Customer Success for two years, and I was actually about to accept another offer when WalkMe reached out. We moved quickly, completing the interview process in just 48 hours. Before I knew it, I had signed the offer, and my WalkMe journey had officially begun. My first role was as a Customer Success Manager, helping customers implement WalkMe and extract real value from the product. Table of Contents hide Climbing, pivoting, and growing Milestones that matter Growth that fuels leadership Why I’ve stayed Looking ahead Climbing, pivoting, and growing From day one, I’ve stayed rooted in Customer Success, but my path hasn’t been a straight line. And I’m grateful for that. After about a year, I became a Team Lead, supporting a growing team of CSMs and WalkMe Builders in our newly launched Raleigh office. That role quickly expanded into leading a team in New York during a time of massive company growth. Back then, we didn’t yet have a formal Professional Services team, so each CS team acted as both CS and PS. That meant I was learning how to lead both relationship-focused and technical individuals. This unique experience that gave me a deeper understanding of how different parts of the business work together. Later, I made the intentional decision to take what I call a “leadership hiatus,” stepping into an Account Manager role to get back into the details and sharpen my skills. That shift helped me reconnect with the product and see our customers in a new way. I had a lot of success there and eventually transitioned back into a Principal CSM role, where I led some of our top accounts and mentored emerging talent. Eventually, I returned to leadership: first managing our Strategic CS team, then AMER West, and today, I’m proud to serve as VP of Customer Success in North America, overseeing both our Customer Success and Customer Solutions teams. Milestones that matter There are many moments I could point to, but for me, it’s not about one milestone. What matters most is being part of building a company we can all be proud of. WalkMe is ever-evolving, ever-changing. That constant momentum can feel chaotic at times, but for the right people, it’s an incredible place to thrive, learn, and make a lasting impact. That said, I’ll never forget the experience of getting to our IPO. The amount of energy, collaboration, and effort it took to reach that moment is hard to describe. A lot of blood, sweat, and tears went into achieving what we did, and I feel lucky to have gone through it with the incredible people who made it happen. Growth that fuels leadership WalkMe has supported my growth in ways that have shaped me as a leader. I’ve had managers who put me in uncomfortable situations that forced me to grow, and I’ve learned to embrace that discomfort as a sign of progress. I’ve also had access to leadership courses, professional coaches, and opportunities that pushed me to expand my skills well beyond being a “WalkMe expert.” That support has shaped not just my career, but who I am as a leader. Why I’ve stayed It comes down to two things: the people and the product. WalkMe is filled with people who work with urgency, care deeply about our success, and genuinely want to win together. That kind of culture is rare. And the product? I’ve seen firsthand how it can drive positive outcomes in infinite ways — across CRMs, HR platforms, eCommerce, and more. Yes, it can be challenging when you’re working with customers on an e-commerce platform, CRM, HRM, and ERP all in the same day. It can take a toll when you’re first getting started. But once you hit your stride and develop your skillset, you become a true jack of all trades. No two days are ever the same, and you’ll never have a boring day. Looking ahead My goal right now is simple: maximize the potential of my team and this company. If we keep focusing on doing that well today, where I end up in 5 to 10 years will take care of itself. More than anything, I want WalkMe to continue growing while remaining a place where people want to stay and grow. Just like I have. How would I summarize my WalkMe journey? A career shaped by learning, built through grit, and defined by the people I’ve been lucky enough to grow with. Want to join Nate and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: Building a market, a team, and a vision - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: Building a market, a team, and a vision By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Kazuhisa Takeya, Director of Sales, Japan When I first joined WalkMe, I was part of the Sales team, focused on connecting customers with a product I believed in. Over time, my role evolved in unexpected ways, not only in title but in impact. I became increasingly drawn to building systems, shaping teams, and helping define how we worked as an organization. That growth led to one of the biggest turning points in my career: my promotion to manager. It was a milestone that reflected more than performance. It was about trust. The company saw potential in me and gave me the support and autonomy to lead, solve challenges, and collaborate with global teams. That support shaped who I am today. Table of Contents hide The moment everything clicked Creating the market, together Looking ahead The moment everything clicked One moment I will never forget is closing my first Enterprise License Agreement. That deal was not just about revenue. It was proof that customers in Japan were beginning to understand the value of Digital Adoption Platforms. Being part of that shift and helping to grow awareness in the Japanese market is something I am deeply proud of. It felt like we were doing something bigger than selling software. We were creating understanding around something entirely new. Creating the market, together Why have I stayed at WalkMe for six years? Because I believe we are building the market ourselves. Every day I feel a strong sense of purpose and fulfillment. There is still so much more I want to do, and so much potential ahead. Not only for me, but for the impact we can make on our customers. What makes this possible is WalkMe’s culture of agility and encouragement. Even as a smaller team in Japan, we are empowered to challenge the status quo, take ownership, and get the support we need quickly and flexibly. That mindset has only strengthened my motivation to serve our customers with everything I have. Looking ahead In the next 5 to 10 years, I see myself becoming a true expert in helping customers leverage generative AI. The possibilities are immense, and I’m excited to be part of that transformation. I want to continue growing side by side with my colleagues, who inspire me daily, and keep achieving meaningful success as a team. How would I summarize my WalkMe journey? I played a part in creating the DAP market. And that’s something I’ll always be proud of. Want to join Kazuhisa and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From CSM to strategist and back again - WalkMe Blog Home » WalkMe Company News Career Spotlight: From CSM to strategist and back again By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Elizabeth Good, Senior Strategic Customer Success Manager I joined WalkMe in 2018 as a Customer Success Manager in our San Francisco office, supporting Strategic accounts. At first, I was very much a jack of all trades, managing onboarding, driving adoption, and helping customers build digital adoption strategies. As I grew in the role, I moved into more specialized positions. I became a Digital Adoption Consultant, then joined the Program Architect team, helping enterprise clients scale WalkMe with long-term governance and expansion strategies. I even spent a year in Services before returning to Customer Success, this time as a Senior CSM bringing a full toolbox of cross-functional experience. Table of Contents hide The Moments That Made It Real Support, Culture, and Growth Looking Ahead The Moments That Made It Real One of the earliest “pinch me” moments came just a month into the job, when I was handed a major, household-name account. By November, I had led a two-day onsite that ultimately helped secure a $1.5M+ renewal. That experience taught me I was more capable than I thought, and I’ve carried that confidence into every challenge since. More recently, I was honored to receive the Top CSM award for North America and celebrated the moment at President’s Club in Thailand. That recognition, along with the “Master of Adoption” award, reminded me how far I’ve come and how supported I’ve been along the way. Support, Culture, and Growth WalkMe has supported my growth not just through diverse accounts and projects, but by investing in my development. I’ve benefited from coaching programs, ERG involvement, and leadership development resources like BetterUp, WalkMe’s coaching offering. These experiences helped me build confidence, navigate change, and stay flexible through transitions, an IPO, a pandemic, and an acquisition. What’s kept me here for nearly a decade? A big part of it is the people — smart, kind, motivated teammates who’ve become close friends. I also appreciate WalkMe’s culture of encouraging exploration, where switching roles or departments is seen as a way to grow, not start over. Looking Ahead In the next few years, I hope to grow into a Principal CSM role. I love the variety this work brings, and I’m especially drawn to the human side — figuring out what drives each client and building strategies that spark real engagement. Outside of work, I’m exploring how AI and automation can support both personal and professional projects. From staying organized at work to building open-source tools that blend design and data, I’ve found AI to be a surprisingly empowering way to stretch my skills and curiosity. My goal at WalkMe is simple: leave things better than I found them. Whether that’s a process, a project, or a customer experience, if I can make it smoother and more thoughtful for the next person, that’s a win. “It began, as many adventures do, with mild confusion and a vague sense of direction — and yet somehow resulted in competence, camaraderie, and the occasional award.” Want to join Elizabeth and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From Recruiting Coordinator to HR Specialist - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: From Recruiting Coordinator to HR Specialist By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Jenn Whiteman, People Operations Lead When I joined WalkMe in September 2018 as a Recruitment Coordinator, I was supporting five recruiters with everything from scheduling interviews to sourcing candidates and managing the overall candidate experience. It was fast-paced and people-focused, the perfect foundation for a career I’ve been building ever since. After about a year and a half, I transitioned into a full-cycle Recruiter role, managing the hiring process from end to end. Not long after that, a new opportunity opened on the People Business Partner team for an HR Coordinator, and I knew I had to go for it. That role marked the beginning of a new chapter. Since joining the HR Operations team, my role has evolved into that of an HR Specialist, where I support WalkMe employees globally through every stage of their employee lifecycle. Over three years in, the growth hasn’t stopped. Each new challenge has expanded my skills and deepened my impact. Table of Contents hide A project that made a difference Growing with the right people around me Looking Ahead A project that made a difference One of the achievements I’m most proud of is leading the revamp of WalkMe’s Global Onboarding program. Two years ago, I noticed our onboarding processes varied across regions, and key stakeholders weren’t fully aligned. I took the lead in standardizing onboarding globally, introducing structured touchpoints, strengthening the buddy system, and launching live HR-led onboarding sessions. The result was a more cohesive, engaging, and memorable experience for every new hire, and stronger cross-functional collaboration across the company. Growing with the right people around me Throughout my journey, I’ve had the unwavering support of our HR leadership team. They’ve pushed me to try new things, provided mentorship, and opened doors for me to take on meaningful work. I’ve always felt that my growth was a shared goal, and that’s made a real difference. What’s kept me here for over seven years? Opportunity and people. WalkMe has given me space to learn, challenge myself, and grow in directions I never expected. And the team is incredible — curious, driven, and creative. These are the kind of people who inspire you to show up as your best self every day. Looking Ahead Our global HR team continues to grow (it’s tripled in size since I joined), and I’m excited about the new areas of HR I’ll get to explore. There’s still so much to learn, and I’m looking forward to stretching my skill set alongside a team that’s always evolving. It’s been about learning to navigate change with curiosity, staying adaptable, and growing alongside ever-evolving business needs. And I can’t wait to see where the journey goes next. jobs.title: 02 How it works
jobs.description: Offer AI that works for people and not the other way around. Request a demo Problem Most GenAI initiatives won't deliver on the promise. Despite the hype of being "easy to use," GenAI requires learning new skills and integrating it into daily workflows. Today’s AI tools use a pull model, demanding users to actively seek help and provide the context. Plus, doing this with dozens of AI tools across apps creates disjointed experiences that add friction. The result? Only a select few will truly adopt, hindering widespread business impact. People, not technology or data are the key to succeeding with AI* * Forrester Research, Prepare Your Entire Workforce For AI Now, March 2024. To make AI work seamlessly for people, it needs to understand context. Who is the person? What are they trying to do? Where did they come from? What workflow are they performing? Where are they going? Solution Contextual AI assistance that meets users where they are. Always present across every application and workflow—no prompting, no switching required. It‘s AI assistance that understands what’s happening on the screen and anticipates the next best move, delivering help exactly when and where your users need it most. Learn more Turn GenAI promise into reality. Help all your people truly transform how they work so GenAI can move the needle for your business. Business value Democratize AI Make it easier for everyone to participate in the GenAI transformation. Gain a competitive edge Reduce risk The WalkMe difference The most qualified provider of AI assistance. Unique data set WalkMe has data that no one else has. We process over 7 billion interactions between people and software every year. 7 billion+ Interactions every year Contextual by design We have a unique understanding of how humans interact with technology and a contextual awareness across workflows and applications. DeepUI Proprietary AI technology Market expertise We know a thing or two about helping boost productivity through guided experiences at the moment of need. It’s what we’ve been doing for more than a decade. 1600+ Global customers Request a demo Additional resources SOLUTION OVERVIEW WalkMe for AI Transformation: Evolve from digital to artificial Learn more REPORT The State of Digital Adoption 2026: The AI Reality Check Read now EBOOK 5 ways to master AI adoption in the workplace Read now

jobs.title: 03 Pinned AI
jobs.description: Skip to content PINNED AI Put AI exactly where employees need it. Process errors grow in silence: an incorrect field, a failed requirement, a step skipped under pressure. Catch them the moment they start, right where the work happens, so they never surface downstream as rework, rejections, or compliance gaps. Request a demo AI SMARTTIPS Catch mistakes before they compound. Free-text is where process discipline breaks down: users type what they know, miss a requirement, and submit. AI SmartTips validate entries against your criteria and policies, flag gaps, and suggest a fix. Catch the problem before submission, and skip the review cycle. SMART HIGHLIGHTS Full context without switching tabs. Important context often sits in another tab, so people either go find it or skip it. Smart Highlights bring that information straight into view, so nothing gets missed and no one has to decide without the full picture. AI LAUNCHERS Trigger AI at the right moment. No user prompting required. AI only works if it’s already where your team works. AI Launchers read the screen and your policies, then produce guidance right when it’s needed. Decide when they fire in plain language, no complex rules needed. Employees stay compliant, without memorizing every policy. AI STEPS IN SMART WALK-THRUS Guarantee AI acts the instant it’s needed. A regular step in a Smart Walk-Thru advances on a click or a text entry, without evaluating context. An AI Step draws on the screen, your knowledge sources, and everything that’s happened so far in that Smart Walk-Thru, so help shows up the instant it’s needed. No prompt to remember, no AI to go find. KNOWLEDGE SOURCE REFERENCING Ground every Pinned AI experience in your knowledge. Generic AI only knows general best practices. Knowledge Source Referencing links it to your policies and SOPs, so AI SmartTips and AI Launchers always match what’s approved. Update the source once, and it’s current everywhere, with nothing left outdated. PINNED AI ANALYTICS Watch what’s landing. Know where to act next. Building Pinned AI experiences is one thing. Knowing they’re working is another. WalkMe analytics show adoption across your organization. Drill deeper with dedicated views for AI SmartTips, Smart Highlights, and more, each built around relevant metrics, so you know exactly what to prioritize. AI belongs in the flow of work. Most applications don’t put it there. 37% of workers skip AI entirely because it breaks their workflow. Pinned AI is a persistent AI assistant that lives inside your enterprise applications. As part of WalkMe’s Contextual AI Assistance suite, it delivers always-on, contextual AI in the flow of work, at the exact field, step, or screen where an issue starts. How is Pinned AI different from standard WalkMe SmartTips and guidance? Standard SmartTips show static guidance on a form field. AI SmartTips evaluate what the user actually typed, compare it against your validation criteria and connected policy documents, and provide specific, real-time revision suggestions. jobs.title: 04 Proactive AI
jobs.description: Skip to content PROACTIVE AI Deliver AI that acts before users ask. Most AI tools rely on employees finding them and knowing what to ask. Proactive AI steps in before anyone has to ask, keeping work on track. Request a demo ACTION BAR Deploy AI that goes wherever work happens. AI usually lives inside separate apps: one for the CRM, another for ticketing, a third for your ERP. The Action Bar brings it all together in one unified experience that follows you across every app, giving employees the right AI help wherever they work. AI LAUNCHERS Suggest the right next action. No prompting required. Employees need assertive and well-timed assistance. AI Launchers read the screen and your policies. Then surface the right action in the Action Bar, the instant it’s relevant, in any application, giving employees confident guidance wherever they’re working. AI DISPLAY CONDITIONS Decide when proactive help appears. Skip rigid rule-writing. Rule-based display logic can’t account for every possible scenario on screen. AI display conditions can. Using natural language prompts, they evaluate what’s happening in real-time, then decide what to show in the Action Bar to best help the user, without the complex rules. MEMORY Make Memory drive action, not just responses. AI usually remembers just enough to personalize a response inside that one tool. Memory in the Action Bar goes further: what’s saved is carried across every application and fed into AI Display Conditions and AI Launchers. So Memory shapes what AI says and does next. WALKME AI SKILLS Bring generative reading and writing into every app. Without a built-in option, employees switch tabs to outside AI tools to proofread an email or shorten a report, losing context on the way. WalkMe’s own AI skills bring proofreading, tone changes, and translation into the Action Bar, without configuring or licensing another tool. CUSTOM ACTIONS Custom prompts built by your users, available everywhere. No builder can predict every prompt a user will need. The Quick Action Screen lets users write and run any prompt in the Action Bar, selecting the page, a specific field, or highlighted text as context. Saved custom actions are available across every app, never written twice. PROACTIVE AI ANALYTICS Track Action Bar usage all the way to outcomes. Clicks are easy to count. Outcomes aren’t. The Action Bar Dashboard tracks usage across your entire organization and shows whether interactions produced a result. Drill into Action Bar adoption and performance, by system and over time, so you know where to act next. AI investment is scaling. Successful outcomes aren’t. 77% of leaders say adoption, not tools, is their primary AI challenge. jobs.title: 05 On-demand AI
jobs.description: Skip to content ON-DEMAND AI Ask AI anything, get an answer, and the next step. Most AI chats live in their own worlds, so employees have to stop and switch just to ask. WalkMe’s On-Demand AI meets users where they’re working, delivering contextual answers and actions grounded in your organization’s knowledge, so it actually gets used. Request a demo AI CHAT Route every question to the right AI, automatically. Different questions need different AI, forcing users to figure out which one to open. AI Chat works differently. Users ask in plain language, in whatever app they’re working in. Smart Routing finds the right AI, AI Answers, ActionBot, or another connected bot, no guessing required. AI ANSWERS Ground answers in your own knowledge, not just the open web. Generic AI answers from the open web, not your policies or process. AI Answers searches your organization’s knowledge first, turning to the web only when needed and allowed. Admins control which sources feed it, so answers stay grounded in what’s approved. AI IN ACTIONBOT Replace scripted chats with conversations that adapt. Automated conversations follow the same script, asking the same questions no matter what employees actually need. ActionBot has a real conversation instead. Set the goal, and it handles the rest, adapting to what employees say and getting things done along the way. TEXT-TO-ACTION Turn a chat answer into the next step, automatically. A good answer that ends the conversation still leaves the task undone. AI Chat connects directly to WalkMe guidance and automation, so a response can trigger a Smart Walk-Thru, launch ActionBot, or surface the next best action. Users don’t copy an answer into another tool. They keep moving. PERSISTENT CHAT CONTEXT Carry the conversation across every app, not just one. AI chat tools often live in one destination, so a conversation resets the moment employees switch to a different work application. WalkMe’s AI Chat maintains persistent context and history, so conversations keep running wherever employees go, and users never start over. ON-DEMAND AI ANALYTICS Measure what employees ask, and whether AI Chat delivers. Rolling out AI Chat is one thing. Knowing it’s working is another. WalkMe analytics groups every question by topic, so you see what employees need help with. Drill into individual answers to catch knowledge gaps before they repeat, and see usage by feature and system, so you know where it’s paying off. Employees already ask AI for help, whether it’s approved or not. 45% of workers used an unapproved AI tool in the past 30 days, many with confidential data.
